WHAT WILL YOU DO IN THIS ROLE? ICEYE is seeking a Mechanical AIT (Assembly, Integration & Testing) Engineer to own the mechanical side of production end to end -- integration, testing, supplier selection, continuous improvement, and adapting processes as new designs come through. In this role, you will be the technical expert responsible for satellite mechanical integration and vibration testing, ensuring that the structure, payload, solar arrays, propulsion and thermal hardware come together as a flight-ready unit that survives launch. You will act as the primary technical contact for mechanical integration issues and drive improvements in build cycle time, test efficiency and build reliability, ensuring every spacecraft meets ICEYE’s high standards for reliability and mission success. Key Responsibilities - Lead the mechanical integration of the satellite (structure, payload, solar arrays, propulsion, harness routing, thermal hardware), including torque control, bonding, alignment and mass properties measurements - Own vibration test campaigns end to end: test specification, fixtures, instrumentation, execution, data analysis and reporting, with test levels and FEM correlation defined together with Structures Engineering - Act as primary technical contact for mechanical integration issues, performing root cause analysis on nonconformances and coordinating with Mechanical/Structures Engineering to resolve anomalies - Survey, evaluate and select suppliers and test facilities for mechanical parts, MGSE and fixtures, including audits and first article inspections - Contribute to and improve AIT documentation, including mechanical integration procedures, test plans and as-built configuration records - Interface with Global AIT, Mechanical/Structures Engineering, QA and Launch teams to ensure alignment on product standards and lessons learned - Drive continuous improvement and automation in mechanical integration methods, test data processing and build cy

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR Must haves: - Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or related field - Experience in aerospace, automotive, or related industries - Experience in designing satellites structures, subsystems or similar complex electromechanical systems - Understanding of mechanical stress, vibration, and thermal effects on space structures & mechanisms - Ability to work cross-functionally with systems, electrical, and manufacturing teams - Familiarity with industry standards such as ECSS, NASA, MIL - Strong team working, analytical, documentation, and communication skills - Ability to make multi team and organisational impact Nice to haves: - Experience with PLM/PDM systems for configuration control - Hands-on experience with mechanical systems assembly, integration, and testing - Prior experience with launch vehicle or spacecraft environments (SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ESA, etc.) APPLICATION PROCESS - Talent Attraction Introduction - Hiring Manager Alignment - Task Assignment - Technical Interview - Director Interview WORKING AT ICEYE At ICEYE, you’ll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. This role directly contributes to ICEYE’s ambition to become the leading provider of space-based ISR infrastructure by scaling reliable, high-impact mission delivery globally. WHO WE ARE ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth. ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system. ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future. Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. ...er company policy (up to 2 days/week remote); in practice, this hands-on, technical-managerial role requires being onsite at our Valencia office most of the time - Employment is subject to applicable security screening WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS You own the end-to-end build, integration, testing and delivery of the developmental satellites, starting with early preparation and alignment with designers, procurement and operations teams, through the Qualification Model (QM) and Flight Model (FM). You plan the AIT timeline, lead the build team, and keep build documentation, configuration tracking and lessons learned flowing back to designers, so every future unit is faster and easier to build. This position sits within the Testing Team. It is important to note that this is developmental, prototype satellite work rather than repeat-production integration: requirements are not yet frozen, designs evolve frequently, and the Lead is expected to resolve novel problems rather than execute a fixed procedure. WHO WE ARE ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations, including sovereign and turnkey ISR missions built on ICEYE's world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, alongside access to data from the world's largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities let partners detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth, day or night and in any weather, with ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits. As a trusted partner for defence, intelligence, security and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE's near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
